_name_note: Guppy and GUPPI are both canon and they are not the same thing. GUPPI is the interface — first named in Bk1 ch2, before Bob can speak, when he is told it takes a few attempts to mesh — and the books use it 23 times. Guppy, 304 times, is Bob's personification of it: the fish. The Cast of Characters draws the line outright, and adds that different Bobs give Guppy different system resources, which is why their Guppys behave differently. The expansion, General Unit Primary Peripheral Interface, is in book 4's List of Acronyms and nowhere else — it is the one term book 4 adds that book 2 does not have. This registry says Guppy throughout, which is right: what runs this console is a personification, not a peripheral.
_comment: Guppy, the ship's AI. The books say he looks like Admiral Ackbar — a Star Wars character we can't reproduce — so this is built from what that description implies rather than from the reference: a tall smooth cranium, eyes mounted on bulges that break the silhouette at the sides, a broad jowly lower face and a wide downturned mouth. The first attempt sank the eyes into a rounded skull and came out looking like a grey alien; eyes protruding past the outline is the single feature that makes it read as amphibian.
_palette_note: fill-opacity against currentColor, not colours, so one portrait works wherever it lands. P is the eyeball, brighter than skin so the bulges read as spheres; d is the pupil, nearly transparent so it reads as depth on a dark panel.
